oliver: Heads up — observed a recurring OOM on canary after the kernel-selector refactor. Happens when a long chat session (KV cache > 1.2M entries) hits the logits path. stacktrace-ish log below from the canary host:

oliver: ```
[2025-06-10T13:12:03Z] ERR gpu_memory: allocation failed: cudaMalloc 134217728 bytes
[2025-06-10T13:12:03Z] WARN runtime: attempted reuse of buffer id=0x7f8c2a (expected free)
[2025-06-10T13:12:03Z] INFO kvcache: active_keys=1_234_567 streams=8
```

nina: Oof. Does it reproduce locally with the new kernel affinity?

oliver: Yes, repros with --profile and parallel streams=8. If I force the old kernel selector, no OOM. The kicker: allocator reports buffer as free but the stream still has a pending kernel referencing it (zombie state).

sara: Sounds like a lifetime mismatch between the slab allocator and stream fences. We kept optimistic reuse to avoid syncs; maybe the refactor changed ordering of stream callbacks.

miguel: Can you paste the short repro command? I'll run our debug harness on an ampere instance.

oliver: Repro command:

oliver: ```bash
./run_canary --model=xl-8k --streams=8 --context=8192 --kv-ops=heavy --profile=nvtx --kernel-selector=refactor
```

oliver: Quick profiling note: nvprof shows spikes where a reuse hit coincides with a kernel launch latency jump and then a subsequent allocation failure. Looks like the buffer was recycled immediately but still referenced on a different CUDA stream.

nina: Proposed mitigation options:
1) Add a light-weight lease token stamped to buffers; only allow reuse after cross-stream fence confirms completion.
2) Keep optimistic reuse for intra-stream only; fallback to conservative for cross-streams.
3) Add short-lived per-request scratch buffers for logits when KV-depth > threshold.

sara: I like 1 + 3. Lease tokens give us a repro-friendly invariant and 3 avoids global perf impact for the heavy-tail sessions.

miguel: Agree. Also we should add a reconciler task that periodically scans the allocator free lists vs stream outstanding operations and logs inconsistencies (count of "zombie" buffers). That would help root cause binary search in nightly runs.

oliver: I sketched a reconciler PoC that queries CUevent states and marks buffer leases as "pending-return" until event indicates completion. Cheap check every 250ms per-GPU. Perf cost seems negligible on simple runs.

oliver: PoC snippet (pseudo):

oliver: ```cpp
for (auto &lease : active_leases) {
  if (!lease.fence.recorded) continue;
  if (cuEventQuery(lease.fence.event) == CUDA_SUCCESS) {
     allocator.mark_free(lease.buf);
  } else {
     stats.zombie_count++;
  }
}
```

nina: Nice. We need the reconciler metrics exported: zombie_count, reconciler_latency_ms, leases_pending. Add an alert if zombie_count > 10 for 1m on any host.

ci-bot: nightly-canary: perf/regressions: tail-latency +6.1% on canary after kernel-selector merge; OOM incidents=3 (see run 2025-06-09-23).

sara: +6% tail is alarming but consistent with the reuse bug. Plan: revert kernel-selector change in canary, land reconciler + lease tokens behind a feature flag, then run 24h canary with KV stress harness.

miguel: For the lease token design, think about the metadata size. We should avoid per-buffer heap allocations. Make lease struct compact (uint64 token, uint32 stream_id, uint8 state). Also ensure cache-line friendly access when scanning.

oliver: I'll open a draft PR with the reconciler and the feature-flagged lease tokens. Will wire metrics and a test harness that asserts no buffer is marked free while its event is pending.

nina: Add a fuzz test that interleaves stream launches and artificial delays to catch races.

sara: Also add a quick fix for space: when KV-depth > 1M, prefer allocating temporary logits via a small per-request arena (64MB cap) before touching the global pool. That prevents a single long session from starving shared slabs.

oliver: Sounds good. I'll post the PR link when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
